title: Through Thee as We Together Came
description: Through Thee as We Together Came in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 163, “Parting Hymn”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Through thee as we to-ge-ther came, In sin-gle-ness of heart, And met, O Je-sus! in thy name, So in thy name we part.

lines: Through thee as we together came,
And met, O Jesus! in thy name,
So in thy name we part.
Nearer to thee our spirits lead,
Till thou hast made us free indeed,
When to the right or left we stray,
But guide our feet into the way

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
